subject: Need help: occu() error when specifying observation-level covariate

messages.author: 79b517e9298a19fe
messages.subject: Need help: occu() error when specifying observation-level covariate
parts:
Hello,

I have an unmarkedFrameOccu() object called "occu_object" that looks like this:

> summary(occu_object)
unmarkedFrame Object

60 sites
Maximum number of observations per site: 120
Mean number of observations per site: 120
Sites with at least one detection: 12

Tabulation of y observations:
   0    1
7043  157

Site-level covariates:
   site_cov_1      
 Min.   :-2.21687  
 1st Qu.:-0.77791  
 Median :-0.05893  
 Mean   :-0.05834  
 3rd Qu.: 0.73253  
 Max.   : 2.15004  

Observation-level covariates:
   obs_cov_1      
 Min.   :-3.73887  
 1st Qu.:-0.65971  
 Median : 0.02143  
 Mean   : 0.01381  
 3rd Qu.: 0.68913  
 Max.   : 3.52300


As you can see it has both site- and observation-level covariates (called "site_cov_1" and "obs_cov_1" respectively).

Using occu() to fit the data works when I specify the site-level covariate like so:

> occu(formula = ~1 ~site_cov_1, data = occu_object


However, occu() gives me an object not found error when I try to specify my observation level covariate:

> occu(formula = ~1 ~obs_cov_1, data = occu_object)
Error in eval(predvars, data, env) : object 'obs_cov_1' not found

I can't figure out what's wrong. Can someone please advise on why this happens? Thanks so much!!

messages.subject: Re: Need help: occu() error when specifying observation-level covariate

messages.author: 40e173783f466ae0
messages.subject: Re: Need help: occu() error when specifying observation-level covariate
parts: No, occupancy is assumed to be constant across the visits. So having a covariate that changes each visit for occupancy won't do anything. Detection can vary due to covariates that are constant among visits at a site or otherwise considered a site attribute, which is why I'm guessing you can make the site_cov part of the detection model.
